correctness.rationale: The parity of the total number of ones permits only zero or two; the zero-only count is floor(max(a,b,c)/2). Each distinct two-one factor is encoded uniquely by its outer gaps (i,k), and its halves contain one one each iff i+k≡b mod 2 and |i−k|≤b. The alternating row and column sums give the stated rectangle parity term. In the corner i−k>b put i=k+b+2r, r≥1; counting all k≥0 and removing k≥c+1 gives H(a−b)−H(a−b−c−1), and the other corner is disjoint and symmetric. This also covers zero gaps and the word 11. Uniform row parity and area comparison incurs O(a+b+c+1) error. With s=a+b+c and a≤c, for b≤a and h=c−a the strip-area deficit from s²/8 is 2(b−s/4)²+[h²−(h−b)₊²]/2. For b>a and a>0, area ≤ac<a(s−2a)≤s²/8, with zero area if a=0. Hence the unique positive-sum maximizing proportions are (3/8,1/4,3/8). Continuity and compactness give rigidity for all asymptotically maximizing sequences, not just exact maximizers. For gaps (3t,2t,3t), summing even-difference diagonals gives 4t²+3t+1 two-one factors, to which floor(3t/2) must be added; padding outer zeros gives the lower bound at intermediate lengths. A separate direct substring enumeration on all 2197 triples with 0≤a,b,c≤12 corroborated the formula; the supplied scripts were inspected, not executed. Neither the enumeration nor the Finding claims a finite maximum formula.
